chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Howard McGhee and Brew Moore on "Cubop City"
summary: Machito says Roost label partners Teddy Reig, Morris Levy and Symphony Sid paired McGhee and Moore against the complicated rhythm.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay. Symphony Sid coined the word then, Afro-Cubop, and that's what it was known as, Cubop. Who selected Brew Moore and Howard McGhee to record that?
Well, in those days, Howard McGhee was in his best and Brew Moore start coming up very strongly. He played very nice and ......

Did anybody suggest that these musicians record with the Machito orchestra?; because the Roost label belonged to Morris Levy, to Teddy Reig, to Jack Cook and Symphony Sid. They were four partners in that label and in Bop City and the Royal Roost. Did any of them suggest Howard Mcghee and Brew Moore? Brew Moore is a white Jewish musician, Howard McGhee is an Afro-American, they fitted-in so well on that recording that they have a lot of Afro-Cuban in them. Wouldn't you say?

Well, you name me four guys that was involved with jazz all their lives. The young one was Morris Levy, very talented, a good promoter, a good - he had idea of what-- He had a good idea of marketing as good as Symphony Sid and the other guy and the other guy, because - and what you call it, the first fellow, ahhh ....

Teddy Reig. Teddy Reig was a jitterbug dancer since nineteen, since opened, the Savoy was opened. He used to go up there every night, so he was jazz-inclined all his life, so he had an idea, almost perfect idea, who played good jazz. So that was a good combination between Teddy Reig, Symphony Sid, a good radio disk jockey. He know what he was talking about. He know about that particular music, very well; so Brew Moore was coming up, a young musician, with good ideas, and Howard McGhee was already established. So it was a good combination put Howard McGhee and Brew Moore together with our background. Our background was so excited, so right for dance.

And they happened to be lucky they was very flexible too, because almost was a contradiction to put a tenor-sax and a trumpet player playing against our rhythm that is so complicated. Is complicated for the people that play. (chuckle)
